title: Governance gateways: go/no-go matrix and staged rollback scripts
creator: Jonah Lee
description: Create a concise, operational go/no-go decision matrix and a set of staged rollback scripts and comms templates for the runtime-1.22 launch. This ticket bundles the governance checks that must be executed during pre-launch window, the detailed automated and manual rollback steps, and clear incident/stakeholder messaging for each stage. Goal: reduce cognitive load for on-call and launch leads during production anomalies and enable a <30 minute median decision-to-action time for common failure modes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented go/no-go matrix with measurable signals and owners for each gate; 2) Staged rollback scripts (CLI & playbook) that engineers can execute with documented runbooks and links to GitHub actions/PRs; 3) Three templated comms messages (initial incident, rollback decision, postmortem notice) that PMs/EMs can copy-paste; 4) Runbook has been reviewed by ENG, SRE, Security, and Design and annotated with sign-off comments; 5) Dry-run completed during Launch Readiness drill with <2 observed blockers.
tasks: Draft go/no-go gates and thresholds (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta, canary quality checks)
Author staged rollback scripts: soft-fallback -> model-variant -> full rollback
Create comms templates for incident open / rollback action / stakeholder summary
Link runbook steps to the exact GitHub PRs, dashboard panels (Grafana), and runbook-run commands
Schedule cross-functional review and collect signoffs (SRE, Security, Design, Legal)
Run a tabletop drill with production-like load and record timing/errors
Update release notes guidance with rollback notch and contact list
rollback_plan_summary: Three-stage rollback: 1) Soft-fallback (0–15min): toggle prefix caching and redirect 20% traffic to model-variant 'm-small' via routing policy; 2) Partial rollback (15–45min): scale down runtime-1.22 canary and promote previous stable variant (runtime-1.21) for 50% of traffic, enable conservative batching and disable experimental kernels; 3) Full rollback (45–120min): revert deployment to runtime-1.21, invalidate KV caches, run smoke tests, and confirm SLA metrics before resuming full traffic. Each stage includes exact CLI commands, required approvals, and post-action verification checklist. For each stage we define who can execute (on-call SRE for stage 1, engineering lead + SRE for stage 2, product lead + CTO for stage 3).
go_no_go_matrix: Gate A (Preflight - T-minus 2h): All release-blocking PRs merged (owner: ENG release lead), CI green for main, no outstanding security flags. Gate B (Canary start - T-minus 30m): Health: p50 latency <= +15% of baseline; p99 latency <= +40% of baseline; Error budget consumption < 5% in last 15m. Gate C (Post-canary - T+60m): Quality signals: eval set accuracy within 2% of baseline, user-reported high-severity issues = 0, infra errors < 0.5% of requests. Decision outcomes: GO = all gates pass; HOLD = non-critical signals failing; ABORT = critical blocker (e.g., data exfil risk, security finding, severe latency regression). Owners and escalation path recorded for each gate.
comms_templates: [Initial incident] Subject: [ALERT] runtime-1.22 canary - increased p99 latency. Body: Hi all — The runtime-1.22 canary is showing p99 latency increase of 85% over baseline starting at 14:12 UTC. Impact: degraded response times for ~5% of requests. First action: enabling prefix fallback and throttling burst. Owner: @Aisha (SRE). Will update in 10m with remediation plan.

[Rollback decision] Subject: [ACTION] Rolling back runtime-1.22 to runtime-1.21. Body: We are initiating a staged rollback due to sustained error-rate increase and lower eval quality. Timeline: Stage 1 completed (soft-fallback), proceeding to Stage 2 (partial rollback) now. Expected user-facing impact: minimal; estimated completion: +30m. Owners and contacts: SRE on-call (page), ENG lead (link to PR), Product: @Jonah. Postmortem will follow.

[Stakeholder summary] Subject: Post-rollback summary: runtime-1.22 reversion and next steps. Body: Summary: At 14:45 we reverted to runtime-1.21 after the canary exhibited a quality regression. What happened: short explanation with metrics snapshot. Customer impact: none/minor (choose). Corrective actions: pause kernel change, additional evals, follow-up release timeline. Owner: Product + ENG. Links: incident timeline, Jira/Linear ticket, Slack channel #launch-watcher.
decisions: 1) Use a three-stage rollback instead of immediate full revert to reduce blast radius and avoid user-visible failures. 2) Canary window extended to 60m with automated quality checks. 3) Model-variant routing to be controlled via feature flagging system and must be executable from on-call runbook without code deploy. 4) Only named individuals may approve full rollback (product lead + engineering director).
review_feedback: SRE (Marta Ruiz): requested clearer verification steps for KV cache invalidation and a pre-rollback smoke test. Security (Rahul Mehta): added explicit DO NOT ROLLBACK if a security token rotation is in flight—coordinate with Security Ops. Design (Lina Kim): asked for user-facing messaging templates to include suggested support responses. Action items: add smoke-test script, add check for active key rotations, update support FAQ snippets.
notes: Unique/novel elements: include a short machine-readable JSON snippet at the top of the runbook for automation (see Confluence link). We will also instrument an automatic pager if Gate B exceeds thresholds for two consecutive 5m windows. Plan to run coordinated dry-run on 2026-03-18 09:00 UTC during low-traffic window. Final sign-off checklist will be attached to the release notes before publish.
